description: ClusterLM hardware qualification registry. Every entry requires the physical machines; none may be satisfied by synthetic profiles or simulated network conditions.

experiments.title: Per-machine hardware profile
experiments.purpose: Replace synthetic profile fields with measured values for each execution domain.
machines: Node G14 (Ryzen 9 8945HS, 32 GB, RTX 4070 Laptop 8 GB)
experiments.model: none (synthetic kernels only)
measurements: physical RAM, commit limit, safe allowance under live policy
GPU identity, driver version, DXGI budget / current usage
experiments.decision_affected: HardwareProfile provenance Synthetic -> Measured; admission budgets for every placement.

experiments.title: CPU routed-expert throughput by quant and verification width
experiments.purpose: Measure effective CPU expert bytes/s including unpacking and GEMV for the exact tensor representations.
experiments.command: clusterlm-bench domain cpu-experts --backend strata --model <ultra-dir> --layers 4,20,40 --q 1,2,4 --threads sweep --isa avx2,avx512 --out results/cpu-experts-<machine>.json
machines: Node G14 (Ryzen 9 8945HS, 32 GB, RTX 4070 Laptop 8 GB)
experiments.model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S (selected Ultra artifact, exact shard hashes recorded)
measurements: ms per routed expert per q and quant type
thread-count sweep incl. reserve for service responsiveness
miss-union multiplier on held-out routing traces
experiments.decision_affected: CPU/GPU miss crossover, per-domain expert residency, viability of the stage architecture vs grouped expert domains.

experiments.title: Laptop sustained CPU/GPU performance at thermal equilibrium

measurements: local decode where resident fit is feasible
experiments.decision_affected: P0-E; Strata adapter viability.

experiments.title: Grouped expert-domain barrier cost
experiments.purpose: Measure whether concurrent remote CPU expert work repays 48 per-layer barriers on the real LAN. The clusterlm-expert-domain-bench executable implements the protocol, the Father executor and a Synthetic simulation (fixture model, in-process domains over loopback with simulated links, layer-domain comparison through the Coordinator); it can only emit Synthetic results. A Measured run needs the real-LAN peers and kernels listed in HQ-P0C-02.
machines: Node G14 (Ryzen 9 8945HS, 32 GB, RTX 4070 Laptop 8 GB)
experiments.model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S (selected Ultra artifact, exact shard hashes recorded)
measurements: per-layer barrier RTT (first send to last result, per layer)
messages and bytes per layer and per target pass for q = 1..4
barrier wait versus Father's overlapped local expert work
experiments.decision_affected: Whether the grouped expert-domain or mixed variant proceeds to P0-D.

experiments.title: Grouped expert-domain on real hardware: LAN peers, quantized kernels, real routing
experiments.purpose: Replace the parts of the grouped expert-domain prototype that cannot run in the cloud: expert domains as separate machines reached over the real 1GbE link with mutual TLS (the prototype runs them as threads over loopback), quantized GPU/CPU expert kernels (the prototype runs FP32 reference SwiGLU), and the model's real routing statistics (the analytic model assumes uniform independent routing). Real routing decides how fast the expert union grows with q and how balanced the domains are.
machines: Node G14 (Ryzen 9 8945HS, 32 GB, RTX 4070 Laptop 8 GB)
experiments.model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_S (selected Ultra artifact, exact shard hashes recorded)
measurements: expert-union size per layer and per domain at q = 1..4 under real routing
per-domain share of selections (load imbalance) for range, strided and hot/cold ownership
quantized expert kernel time per distinct expert on each CPU and, for Father, GPU-resident experts
per-layer barrier time and its p95/p99 on the physical LAN
end-to-end emitted tok/s of grouped versus layer-domain on the same model
experiments.decision_affected: Whether the grouped expert-domain topology replaces or complements the layer-domain pipeline, which expert ownership it uses, and the q cap that keeps the expert union affordable.

experiments.title: Tier catalog pinning and context-profile qualification
experiments.purpose: Download and inspect each catalog artifact on Father to pin its manifest root hash, then qualify each offered context profile (4K to 128K) per tier on the real machines so the catalog's qualified flags and readiness notes can change.
experiments.command: clusterlm-bench catalog inspect --model <tier-model-dir> --out results/catalog-<tier>.json && clusterlm-bench catalog contexts --tier <fast|strong|ultra> --contexts 4096,8192,16384,32768,65536,131072 --out results/contexts-<tier>.json
machines: Node G14 (Ryzen 9 8945HS, 32 GB, RTX 4070 Laptop 8 GB)
experiments.model: Fast, Strong and Ultra catalog artifacts (exact shard hashes recorded)
measurements: manifest root hash and exact shard file names/sizes per tier
per context profile: placement feasibility, VRAM/RAM margins, completion without OOM or lease loss
which offered contexts are dropped from the catalog (e.g. Fast 64K/128K)
experiments.decision_affected: Catalog expected_root_hash pinning (pin_status unpinned -> pinned), context profile qualified and offered flags, tier readiness notes.
